summary: Sparse-embedding + gzip chunking causes truncated frames, dropped candidates, and elevated rerank p95
description:
Issue summary: Several customers using sparse embedding payloads report intermittent empty candidate sets and large p95 rerank latencies after switching to client-side gzip compression. Impact: production traffic to the rerank endpoint returns empty candidate arrays for ~0.3% of requests and p95 token latency increases from ~120ms to ~1.3s during these windows. Environment: Dedicated cluster for Lexicon Labs (prod-us-east). This started after the customer's SDK rolled out gzip-by-default for embedding uploads two days ago. Observed with both open-embed-v1 and open-embed-sparse-v1.

Observed behavior: When client sends sparse CSR-like binary frames compressed with Content-Encoding: gzip over HTTP/2 multiplexed connections, the gateway's chunking layer miscalculates frame boundaries for small trailing chunks. The downstream ingest worker interprets a truncated sparse index block as zero-length or wrong-dimension vector, leading to either: (a) candidate suppression (empty result) or (b) a fallback path that converts to dense with zero-padding which causes ANN index fallback and queueing, increasing p95.

Expected behavior: Gateway should correctly decompress and reassemble gzip-compressed frames over HTTP/2 and hand a full, validated embedding payload to the ingest worker. Serving should reject invalid-length embeddings with a 4xx and clear error message rather than silently dropping candidates or falling back to expensive CPU paths.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use the Lexicon SDK with sparse-embed flag enabled and gzip compression on.
2) Send a batch of mixed-size embedding uploads over HTTP/2 to the embedding endpoint with Content-Encoding: gzip and Accept-Encoding headers.
3) Immediately issue a rerank request referencing the new embeddings.
4) Repeat at 200 QPS for 5 minutes to reproduce tail behavior.
5) Observe 503s or empty candidate arrays in ~0.2-0.5% of requests and p95 spikes in serving-runtime.

Deterministic repro in staging: enabled SDK gzip + sparse flag against staging-gateway with http2 multiplexing reproduces sample within 1000 requests. Logs attached below include truncated frame offsets and decoder exceptions.
logs:
[2026-03-10T13:04:12Z] gateway-01 ERROR chunk_reassembly: expected 8192 bytes, got 6104, stream_id=0x7f2a
[2026-03-10T13:04:12Z] ingest-worker WARN sparse-decoder: index-block-truncated, fallback_to_dense=true, embed_id=lex-usr-3482
[2026-03-10T13:04:12Z] serving-runtime ERROR ann-fallback-queueing: worker-saturation, request=rerank/lex-usr-3482, p95=1270ms
[2026-03-10T13:04:13Z] api-gateway INFO request: client-ip=35.200.122.8, method=POST, path=/v1/embeddings, content-encoding=gzip, content-length=0

Note: logs show a content-length mismatch at the gateway (0 after decompress attempt) which correlates to how the HTTP/2 chunking layer interacts with our gzip streaming decoder for small final chunks.
comments: Aisha Kapoor (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer reported sudden regressions after SDK change. Provided initial logs and sample request. Requested immediate triage.

Luis Morales (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging by toggling SDK gzip. Observed truncated index-blocks at gateway; suspect interaction between http2 chunk framing and our in-house gzip streaming wrapper. Kicked to serving-runtime and gateway owners.

Priya Nair (Serving Eng) - 2026-03-11: Found decoder state machine bug when final gzip block size < 1024 bytes under HTTP/2 multiplex path. Created local repro and unit test. Preparing patch to fully buffer final block before handing to sparse decoder.

Aisha Kapoor (Support) - 2026-03-11: Shared workaround to Lexicon Labs: disable SDK gzip or set X-Embed-Format: dense-fp32. Customer applied workaround and saw immediate reduction in empty candidates. Confirmed temporary mitigation acceptable while we push patch.
Luis Morales (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Hotfix PR opened and tested against staging with canary. No regression on dense endpoints. Planning production canary tomorrow (2026-03-13) during low traffic window.
investigation_notes:
Root cause: gzip streaming wrapper in gateway attempted to stream-decompress and incrementally hand bytes to chunk-reassembler for HTTP/2 streams. For sparse payloads (small index blocks appended at the end) the streaming decompressor reports available bytes but final flush sequence was invoked on a later HTTP/2 frame; our chunker considered the frame boundary complete and forwarded a partial payload to the sparse decoder. Sparse decoder treats truncated index blocks as either invalid (silently drop candidate) or attempts CPU fallback by padding to expected length.

Why it's customer-visible: Lexicon uses sparse embedding format that places small index metadata at the tail of the compressed stream; when tail fragments arrive in very small final frames the bug is triggered. Dense embeddings amortize the issue because final blocks are larger. The HTTP/1 path isn't affected; this is limited to HTTP/2+gzip+small-final-frame sequence.

Repro note: Adding an explicit flush in client (larger buffer) or disabling gzip prevents the race. Unit tests added to capture the <1024 byte final-block case for HTTP/2 streams.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation: advised customer to disable client gzip and provided SDK flag to force dense format (X-Embed-Format: dense-fp32). Long-term fix: gateway patch to buffer final decompressed block until Content-Encoding flush confirmed and to validate embedding lengths before forwarding to ingest-worker. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3821 created by Priya Nair. Staging canary passed (2026-03-12). Production canary scheduled for 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC; rollback strategy documented in the linked Confluence runbook. Post-deploy actions: add monitoring alert for chunk_reassembly errors and a synthetic test that sends small-trailing-frame gzip-sparse payloads to staging/production canaries.
